title: Bulls And Cows Score
description: In the guessing game Bulls and Cows, `secret` and `guess` are digit strings of the same length. A bull is a digit that is correct and in the right position. A cow is a digit of the guess that appears in the secret but in a different position (each secret digit can be used only once, and bulls are not counted again as cows). Return the hint as `xAyB` where `x` is the bull count and `y` the cow count.

title: Positional Letter Score
description: Give each lowercase letter a value (`a = 1`, `b = 2`, ..., `z = 26`). A word scores the value of each letter multiplied by its 1-based position in the word. Return the word's score.

title: Nim Opening Win Check
description: In the game of Nim there are piles of stones; players alternate removing any positive number of stones from a single pile, and whoever takes the last stone wins. Return `true` if the player to move can force a win with perfect play.

title: Rock Paper Scissors Points
description: Two players play several rounds of rock-paper-scissors. Round `i` shows `a[i]` for the first player and `b[i]` for the second, with `0 = rock`, `1 = paper`, `2 = scissors` (paper beats rock, scissors beat paper, rock beats scissors). The first player scores `3` for a win, `1` for a draw and `0` for a loss. Return the first player's total.

title: Tennis Game Winner
description: `points` lists who won each point of a tennis game (`A` or `B`). A player wins the game by scoring at least `4` points with a lead of at least `2` over the opponent. Return the winner (`A` or `B`) as soon as the game is decided, or `none` if the points listed do not decide it.
constraints: points contains only A and B

title: Rook Attack Check
description: On an `8 x 8` chessboard (rows and columns numbered `0..7`) a rook stands on `(r1, c1)` and an enemy piece on `(r2, c2)`. There are no other pieces. Return `true` if the rook can capture the piece in one move.

title: Knight Move Check
description: On a chessboard a knight stands on `(r1, c1)`. Return `true` if it can reach `(r2, c2)` in exactly one move (an L-shape: two squares in one direction and one square perpendicular).

title: Bishop Diagonal Check
description: A bishop stands on `(r1, c1)` of an empty chessboard. Return `true` if it can move to `(r2, c2)` in one move (any distance along a diagonal).

title: Disk Seek Distance FIFO
description: A disk head starts at track `start` and serves the requests in `requests` strictly in the given order. Moving between tracks costs the absolute difference of their numbers. Return the total distance travelled by the head.

title: FIFO Page Fault Count
description: Memory has `k` page frames, initially empty. Pages are requested in the order given by `refs`. A request for a page not in memory is a page fault; the page is loaded, evicting the page that has been in memory the longest if all frames are full (FIFO). Return the number of page faults.

title: FCFS Average Waiting Time
description: Processes arrive at times `arrival[i]` (sorted ascending) and need `burst[i]` time units of CPU. The CPU serves them first-come-first-served without interruption; it idles if no process is waiting. A process's waiting time is the gap between its arrival and the moment it starts. Return the average waiting time rounded down.

title: First Fit Allocation Count
description: Memory has blocks of sizes `blocks`. Each process in `procs` (in order) is placed in the first still-free block that is large enough; a block holds at most one process and is then used up. A process that fits nowhere is skipped. Return how many processes were placed.

title: Direct-Mapped Cache Hits
description: A direct-mapped cache has `slots` slots. An address `x` can only live in slot `x % slots`, and each slot stores one address. A request is a hit if its slot already holds exactly that address; otherwise it is a miss and the slot is overwritten with the address. The cache starts empty. Return the number of hits for the request list `addrs`.

title: Call Stack Peak Depth
description: `events` records a program's call stack: `1` means a function was called (depth grows by one) and `-1` means a function returned. The stack starts empty and never becomes negative. Return the greatest depth reached.

examples.explanation: The deepest the stack gets is 2.
The deepest the stack gets is 1.

constraints: each event is 1 or -1 and every prefix sum is >= 0

title: Even Parity Frame Check
description: A transmitted frame is a binary string whose last bit is an even-parity bit: the total number of `1` bits in the whole frame (parity bit included) must be even. Return `true` if the frame passes the parity check.

title: Years To Double Balance
description: A savings account starts with `b` coins and each year gains `r` percent of the current balance, with the gain rounded down to a whole number of coins. Return the number of whole years until the balance is at least twice the starting amount.

title: Progressive Tax Total
description: Income is taxed in brackets. `limits` holds the ascending upper bounds of every bracket except the last one; `rates` holds the tax percentage of each bracket (so `rates.length = limits.length + 1`). The part of the income inside a bracket is taxed at that bracket's rate. Sum the tax of all parts and return the total rounded down to a whole coin.

title: Lowest Running Balance
description: An account starts with `start` coins. `changes` lists deposits (positive) and withdrawals (negative) applied in order. Return the lowest balance the account ever had, including the starting balance.

title: Loan Payoff Months
description: A loan of `P` coins is repaid monthly. Each month interest of `r` percent of the current debt (rounded down) is added and then the payment `pay` is subtracted. The loan is cleared when the debt is `0` or less. Return the number of months needed, or `-1` if the debt never decreases.

examples.explanation: The loan is cleared in 11 month(s) (-1 means never).
The loan is cleared in 1 month(s) (-1 means never).

title: Best Discount Price
description: An item costs `price`. A shop offers two coupons but you may use only one: a percentage coupon that removes `pct` percent of the price (the reduction rounded down) or a flat coupon that removes `flat` coins (the price never drops below `0`). Return the lowest price you can pay.

title: Derangement Count
description: A derangement is a permutation of `1..n` in which no element stays in its original position. Return the number of derangements of `n` elements (`1` for `n = 0`).
constraints: the answer fits in a 32-bit integer

title: Catalan Number
description: The Catalan numbers count, among many things, the binary tree shapes with `n` nodes. They satisfy `C(0) = 1` and `C(n + 1) = sum of C(i) * C(n - i)` for `i` from `0` to `n`. Return `C(n)`.
constraints: the answer fits in a 32-bit integer

title: Binomial Coefficient Value
description: Return `C(n, k)`, the number of ways to choose `k` items out of `n` (order does not matter).
constraints: the answer fits in a 32-bit integer

title: Largest Triangular Index
description: The `k`-th triangular number is `1 + 2 + ... + k`. Return the largest `k` such that the `k`-th triangular number is at most `n`.
constraints: k = 0 corresponds to the empty sum 0

title: Recaman Sequence Term
description: The Recaman sequence starts `a(0) = 0`. For `i >= 1`, `a(i) = a(i - 1) - i` if that value is positive and has not appeared earlier in the sequence; otherwise `a(i) = a(i - 1) + i`. Return `a(n)`.

title: Stern Diatomic Term
description: Stern's diatomic sequence is defined by `s(0) = 0`, `s(1) = 1`, `s(2k) = s(k)` and `s(2k + 1) = s(k) + s(k + 1)`. Return `s(n)`.
constraints: the answer fits in a 32-bit integer

title: Pell Number
description: The Pell numbers are `P(0) = 0`, `P(1) = 1` and `P(n) = 2 * P(n - 1) + P(n - 2)`. Return `P(n)`.
constraints: the answer fits in a 32-bit integer

title: Kolakoski Ones Count
description: The Kolakoski sequence uses only `1` and `2` and describes its own run lengths: it starts `1, 2, 2, 1, 1, 2, 1, 2, 2, 1, ...`, where the lengths of its consecutive runs of equal values are again `1, 2, 2, 1, 1, 2, ...`. Return how many of the first `n` terms equal `1`.

examples.explanation: 1 of the first n terms are 1.
1 of the first n terms are 1.

title: Padovan Number
description: The Padovan sequence is `P(0) = P(1) = P(2) = 1` and `P(n) = P(n - 2) + P(n - 3)`. Return `P(n)`.
constraints: the answer fits in a 32-bit integer

title: Lucky Ticket Check
description: A six-digit ticket number is lucky if the sum of its first three digits equals the sum of its last three digits. Return `true` for a lucky ticket.

title: ISBN-10 Validity
description: An ISBN-10 has ten characters: nine digits followed by a check character that is a digit or `X` (value `10`). It is valid when `10*d1 + 9*d2 + ... + 1*d10` is divisible by `11`. Return `true` if `isbn` is valid.
constraints: the first nine characters are digits; the last is a digit or X

title: Luhn Checksum Valid
description: The Luhn check validates card numbers: from the rightmost digit moving left, double every second digit (the 2nd, 4th, ... from the right); if doubling gives more than `9`, subtract `9`. The number is valid if the sum of all digits after this step is divisible by `10`. Return `true` if `number` is valid.

title: Luhn Check Digit
description: Given the digits `payload` of a card number without its final check digit, return the single digit that must be appended so that the full number passes the Luhn check (double every second digit counting from the right, subtract `9` from doubled values above `9`, total divisible by `10`).

title: EAN-13 Check Digit
description: An EAN-13 barcode has `13` digits; the last one is a check digit. Weight the first twelve digits alternately `1, 3, 1, 3, ...` from the left, add them up, and the check digit is the amount needed to reach the next multiple of `10` (`0` if already a multiple). Given the first twelve digits return the check digit.

title: Shared Permission Bits
description: Two users hold permission masks `a` and `b`, where each set bit grants one permission. Return how many permissions (bits) they both have.
constraints: count the set bits of a AND b

title: Optimal Page Fault Count
description: Memory has `k` frames, initially empty. When a page that is not in memory is requested a page fault occurs; the page is loaded, and if memory is full the page whose next request lies farthest in the future (or that is never requested again) is evicted (Belady's optimal policy). Ties between pages that are never used again may be broken arbitrarily. Return the number of page faults for the request list `refs`.

title: Clock Page Replacement Faults
description: Memory has `k` frames arranged in a circle, each with a reference bit; a clock hand starts at frame `0`. A request for a page in memory sets its bit to `1`. On a page fault the hand sweeps forward: while the frame under the hand is occupied and has bit `1` it clears the bit and moves on; the page is then placed in the frame under the hand (empty or the first one found with bit `0`) with bit `1`, and the hand moves one frame forward. Return the number of page faults.

title: Elevator Sweep Seek Distance
description: A disk head starts at track `start` moving toward higher tracks. It serves every request on tracks `>= start` in ascending order until it reaches the highest requested track, then reverses and serves the remaining requests (tracks `< start`) in descending order, stopping at the lowest one. Return the total distance travelled (LOOK scheduling).

title: Nearest Request Seek Distance
description: A disk head starts at track `start`. It always moves to the pending request with the smallest distance from the current track (if two are equally near, the lower track number wins), serves it, and repeats until nothing is left (SSTF scheduling). Return the total distance travelled.

title: Shortest Job First Average Wait
description: Process `i` arrives at `arrival[i]` and needs `burst[i]` CPU time. Whenever the CPU is free it starts, without interruption, the already-arrived process with the shortest burst (ties go to the lower index); if nothing has arrived it idles until the next arrival. A process's waiting time is the gap between its arrival and its start. Return the average waiting time rounded down.

title: Round Robin Average Wait
description: All processes arrive at time `0` in index order and need `burst[i]` CPU time. The CPU gives each process in the queue up to `q` time units in turn; an unfinished process goes to the back of the queue. A process's waiting time is its finishing time minus its burst. Return the average waiting time rounded down.

title: Banker's Safe State Check
description: A system has `m` resource types; `available[j]` units of type `j` are free. `n` processes each declare a maximum demand `maxNeed` and currently hold `alloc` units (both are flat row-by-row tables of size `n x m`, so `maxNeed[i*m + j]` is the maximum of type `j` for process `i`). A process can finish if its remaining need (`maxNeed - alloc`) fits in the free units; when it finishes it returns everything it holds. Return `true` if all processes can finish in some order.

title: Token Bucket Allowed Requests
description: A token bucket holds at most `C` tokens and starts full. Every second `R` new tokens are added (never exceeding `C`). Requests arrive at the times in `times` (sorted ascending, several may share a second); each request needs one token and is allowed only if a token is available, otherwise it is dropped. Return how many requests are allowed.

title: Bitmap Allocator Replay
description: A bitmap of `N` slots starts all free. `ops` is a flat list of triples `(type, x, y)`. Type `0` (with `y = 0`) allocates `x` consecutive free slots at the lowest possible start index and marks them used; its result is `start + 1`, or `0` if no run of `x` free slots exists. Type `1` frees the `y` slots beginning at index `x` (already-free slots stay free). Return the sum of all allocation results.

examples.explanation: The allocation results add up to 6.
The allocation results add up to 1.

constraints: 3 <= ops.length <= 150 and ops.length is a multiple of 3; indices stay inside the bitmap

title: Best Fit Failed Allocations
description: Memory is a set of free blocks with sizes `blocks`. Each process in `procs` (in order) is placed in the smallest block that is large enough (lowest index on ties); the block shrinks by the process size and may host further processes. A process that fits no block fails. Return the number of failed processes.

title: Wordle Feedback String
description: In Wordle, a guess is compared with the hidden `answer` (same length). A guess letter that matches the answer letter in the same position is `G`. Every other guess letter is `Y` if the answer still has an unmatched copy of that letter elsewhere (each answer letter can justify only one `Y`, and letters are checked left to right), otherwise `B`. Return the feedback string.

title: Connect Four Winner
description: Connect Four is played on a board with `6` rows and `7` columns (columns `0..6`). `moves` lists the column chosen at each turn; players alternate, player `1` first, and a disc falls to the lowest free row of its column. Return `1` or `2` for the first player who gets four discs in a row (horizontally, vertically or diagonally), stopping at that move, or `0` if nobody does after all moves.

examples.explanation: The result is 1 (0 means no winner).
The result is 0 (0 means no winner).

constraints: 0 <= moves[i] <= 6 and no column receives more than 6 discs

title: Minesweeper Flood Reveal
description: `grid` is an `R x C` minefield stored row by row (`1` = mine, `0` = safe). Clicking the safe cell `(r0, c0)` reveals it. A revealed cell with no mines among its eight neighbours also reveals all eight neighbours (and so on, repeatedly). Return the number of cells revealed after the click.
constraints: each cell is 0 or 1; the clicked cell is safe

title: Slide Left Merge Score
description: In the game 2048 a row of tiles is slid to the left: empty cells (`0`) disappear, then neighbouring equal tiles are merged from the left, each tile taking part in at most one merge per slide (so `2 2 2` becomes `4 2`). A merge scores the value of the new tile. Return the total score of one slide of `row`.
constraints: each tile is 0 or a power of two up to 2048

title: Ten-Pin Bowling Score
description: `rolls` lists the pins knocked down by each roll of one complete ten-pin bowling game. A frame is one or two rolls: a strike (`10` on the first roll) ends the frame and scores 10 plus the next two rolls; a spare (two rolls totalling 10) scores 10 plus the next roll; otherwise the frame scores its pins. The tenth frame gives extra rolls after a strike (two) or a spare (one), and those extra rolls only count as bonus for that frame. Return the total score.
constraints: the rolls form a complete, valid game

title: Subtraction Game Grundy Value
description: A heap holds `n` stones. A move removes exactly `m` stones from the heap for some `m` in `moves` (if enough stones remain). The Grundy value of a heap is the smallest non-negative integer that is not the Grundy value of any heap reachable by one move (a heap with no moves has value `0`). Return the Grundy value of the heap of size `n`.

title: Hanoi Disk Peg After K Moves
description: In the Tower of Hanoi, `n` disks (numbered `1` = smallest to `n` = largest) start on peg `0` and must be moved to peg `2` using peg `1` as spare, by the shortest standard solution (which has `2^n - 1` moves and is unique). Return the peg (0, 1 or 2) on which disk `d` rests after exactly `k` moves of that solution.

title: FIFO Cost Of Goods Sold
description: `ops` is a flat list of triples `(type, quantity, price)`. Type `0` buys `quantity` units of stock at `price` each; type `1` sells `quantity` units (its `price` field is `0`). Sold units always come from the oldest purchased units first (FIFO) and a sale never exceeds the stock on hand. Return the total purchase cost of all units that were sold.

examples.explanation: The cost of goods sold is 85.
The cost of goods sold is 3.

constraints: 3 <= ops.length <= 150 and ops.length is a multiple of 3

title: Maximum Sale Revenue
description: A shop stocks coloured balls: `inventory[i]` balls of colour `i`. The price of a ball equals the number of balls of its colour currently in stock, so each sale lowers that colour's price by one. Selling exactly `orders` balls in the best order, return the maximum total revenue (the stock is large enough to cover all orders).

title: Limited Supply Fewest Coins
description: A cashier has `counts[i]` coins of value `values[i]`. Return the fewest coins that add up to exactly `target`, or `-1` if that amount cannot be made.

title: Misere Nim First Player Wins
description: In misere Nim, players alternate removing any positive number of stones from one pile, and the player who takes the last stone LOSES. The first player moves first and both play perfectly. Return `true` if the first player wins. At least one stone is present.
constraints: the total number of stones is at least 1

title: Partitions With Bounded Parts
description: Count the ways to write `n` as a sum of positive integers none larger than `k`, where the order of the summands does not matter (`3 + 1` and `1 + 3` are the same way).
constraints: the answer fits in a 32-bit integer

title: Set Partitions Into K Blocks
description: Count the ways to split a set of `n` distinguishable items into exactly `k` non-empty groups (the groups themselves are not ordered). These are the Stirling numbers of the second kind.
constraints: the answer fits in a 32-bit integer

title: Bell Number
description: Return the number of ways to partition a set of `n` distinguishable items into any number of non-empty, unordered groups (the Bell number `B(n)`, with `B(0) = 1`).
constraints: the answer fits in a 32-bit integer

title: Bounded Height Bracket Strings
description: Count the balanced strings made of `n` pairs of round brackets in which the nesting depth never exceeds `h` (for example `(())` has depth `2`, `()()` has depth `1`).
constraints: 0 <= h <= 15; the answer fits in a 32-bit integer

title: Egyptian Fraction Term Count
description: The greedy method writes a fraction `p / q` (with `0 < p < q`) as a sum of distinct unit fractions: repeatedly subtract the largest unit fraction `1 / d` that does not exceed what is left. Return how many unit fractions the method uses.
constraints: the fraction need not be in lowest terms

title: Stern-Brocot Walk Length
description: The Stern-Brocot tree starts at `1/1`; the left and right children of a node come from taking mediants with its nearest ancestors (the root's bounds are `0/1` and `1/0`, and a mediant of `a/b` and `c/d` is `(a + c)/(b + d)`). Moving to a child counts one step. Return the number of steps from the root `1/1` down to the fraction `p/q` (reduce it to lowest terms first).
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Calkin-Wilf Position
description: The Calkin-Wilf tree has root `1/1`, and node `a/b` has left child `a/(a+b)` and right child `(a+b)/b`. Listing the tree level by level, left to right, numbers the fractions `1, 2, 3, ...` (so `1/1` is 1, `1/2` is 2, `2/1` is 3). Return the position of the fraction `p/q` (reduce it to lowest terms first).
constraints: the position fits in a 32-bit integer

title: Fewest Fibonacci Summands
description: Return the smallest number of Fibonacci numbers (`1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ...`; each value may be used repeatedly) that add up to `n`.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Permutation Lexicographic Rank
description: `perm` is a permutation of `1..n`. List all permutations of `1..n` in dictionary order (as sequences of numbers) and return the 1-based position of `perm` in that list.
constraints: perm contains each of 1..n exactly once

title: Permutation Order
description: `perm` is a permutation of `0..n-1`, meaning position `i` is sent to `perm[i]`. Applying it over and over eventually restores the original arrangement. Return the smallest number of applications `k >= 1` after which every position is back where it started.

examples.explanation: The order of the permutation is 2.
The order of the permutation is 1.

constraints: perm contains each of 0..n-1 exactly once

title: Huffman Merge Cost
description: `freq` lists symbol frequencies. Repeatedly take two nodes of smallest weight, merge them into one node whose weight is their sum, and pay that sum, until a single node is left (Huffman coding). Return the total paid (`0` if there is only one symbol).

title: Roman Numeral Letters Total
description: Write every integer from `1` to `n` as a standard Roman numeral (`4 = IV`, `9 = IX`, `40 = XL`, `90 = XC`, `400 = CD`, `900 = CM`, with `M = 1000`). Return the total number of letters used over all of them.
constraints: All inputs are integers or strings within the stated ranges

title: Group Size Query Replay
description: There are `n` items, each initially alone in its own group. `ops` is a flat list of triples `(type, a, b)`. Type `0` merges the groups containing items `a` and `b`. Type `1` (with `b = 0`) asks for the size of the group containing item `a`. Return the sum of all answers to type-1 operations.

examples.explanation: The queried sizes add up to 4.
The queried sizes add up to 1.

constraints: 3 <= ops.length <= 300 and ops.length is a multiple of 3; 0 <= a, b < n

title: Prefix Counter Replay
description: `ops` is a space-separated list of commands. `+word` stores a word (the same word may be stored several times and every copy counts). `?prefix` asks how many stored copies start with `prefix` at that moment. Return the sum of all `?` answers.
constraints: each word or prefix has 1 to 8 lowercase letters

title: Range Minimum With Updates
description: `arr` is an array. `ops` is a flat list of triples `(type, x, y)`: type `0` sets `arr[x] = y`; type `1` asks for the minimum of `arr[x..y]` (inclusive, `x <= y`). Return the sum of all type-1 answers.

examples.explanation: The minimum queries add up to 4.
The minimum queries add up to 1.

constraints: 3 <= ops.length <= 300 and ops.length is a multiple of 3

title: Cursor Text Editor Replay
description: A text editor starts empty with its cursor at the start. `ops` is a flat list of pairs `(type, x)`. Type `0` types the letter with index `x` (`0 = a`, `1 = b`, ..., `25 = z`) at the cursor, which moves right of it. Type `1` moves the cursor left by `x` positions (stopping at the start). Type `2` moves it right by `x` (stopping at the end). Type `3` deletes up to `x` letters immediately to the left of the cursor. Return the final text.
constraints: type is 0-3; 0 <= x <= 25 for typing, 1 <= x <= 50 otherwise

title: BST Insertion Depth Total
description: Keys are inserted one by one, in the given order, into an initially empty binary search tree (smaller keys go left, larger go right, no rebalancing). The root has depth `0`. Return the sum of the depths of all nodes after all insertions.
constraints: -10^6 <= keys[i] <= 10^6 and all keys are distinct

title: Cartesian Tree Height
description: Build a binary tree from `arr` (distinct values) as follows: the smallest value is the root; the values to its left in the array form its left subtree and the values to its right form its right subtree, built the same way. Return the height of this tree counted in nodes (a single node has height `1`).

title: Week Of Year Number
description: Weeks run from Monday to Sunday, and week `1` of a year is the week that contains 1 January (so it may be a partial week). Given a valid Gregorian date, return its week number within that year. (1 January 1970 was a Thursday.)

title: Shortest Remaining Time Turnaround
description: Process `i` arrives at `arrival[i]` and needs `burst[i]` CPU time. At every moment the CPU runs the arrived, unfinished process with the least remaining time (ties go to the lower index), and a newly arrived process with a smaller remaining time preempts the running one immediately. A process's turnaround time is its finishing time minus its arrival time. Return the sum of all turnaround times.

examples.explanation: The turnaround times add up to 52.
The turnaround times add up to 5.

title: FIFO Anomaly Frame Count
description: With FIFO page replacement, adding memory frames normally reduces page faults, but sometimes it makes them worse (Belady's anomaly). Let `faults(k)` be the number of page faults FIFO produces on `refs` with `k` frames (memory starts empty; the page that has been resident longest is evicted). Return the smallest `k` with `1 <= k < K` such that `faults(k + 1) > faults(k)`, or `-1` if there is none.

examples.explanation: The first anomaly occurs at k = 3 (-1 means none).
The first anomaly occurs at k = -1 (-1 means none).

title: Round Robin Completion Total
description: Process `i` arrives at `arrival[i]` and needs `burst[i]` CPU time. The CPU serves a FIFO queue in round-robin fashion with time slice `q`: it takes the process at the front and runs it for up to `q` units. When a slice ends, processes that have arrived by that moment join the back of the queue first, and then the interrupted process (if unfinished) joins behind them. If the queue is empty the CPU idles until the next arrival. Return the sum of all processes' finishing times.

examples.explanation: The finishing times add up to 38.
The finishing times add up to 7.

title: Tic-Tac-Toe Optimal Outcome
description: A `3 x 3` Tic-Tac-Toe board is given as a 9-character string read row by row (`X`, `O` or `.` for empty). `X` always moves first, so the player to move is `X` when both symbols have appeared equally often, otherwise `O`. If a line is already complete the game is over. Otherwise both players play perfectly (each trying to win, else to draw). Return `1` if `X` ends up winning, `-1` if `O` wins and `0` for a draw.

examples.explanation: The outcome is 0 (1 = X wins, -1 = O wins, 0 = draw).
The outcome is 1 (1 = X wins, -1 = O wins, 0 = draw).

constraints: board.length = 9, only X, O and . appear
the position is reachable in a real game (X moved first) and not won by both players

title: Wythoff Game Opening Win
description: Two piles hold `a` and `b` stones. A move removes any positive number of stones from one pile, or the same positive number from both piles. The player who takes the last stone wins. Return `true` if the player to move can force a win.
constraints: play is perfect on both sides

title: Multi-Heap Subtraction Winner
description: Several heaps of stones are given in `piles`. A move chooses one heap and removes exactly `m` stones from it for some `m` in `moves` (the heap must hold at least `m`). A player who cannot move loses. Return `true` if the player to move wins with perfect play.

title: Buddy Allocator Failed Requests
description: A buddy memory allocator manages `2^k` units, initially one free block at address `0`. An allocation request of `size` is rounded up to the next power of two `s`; it takes the smallest free block of size at least `s` (ties go to the lowest address), and while that block is larger than `s` it is split into two equal halves, keeping the lower half and returning the upper half to the free pool. If no block is large enough the request fails. The allocation operations are numbered `0, 1, 2, ...` in order of appearance (including failed ones). Freeing a block returns it and merges it with its buddy (the equal block whose address differs by that block's size) repeatedly while the buddy is free. `ops` is a flat list of pairs `(type, value)`: type `0` allocates `value` units, type `1` frees the allocation numbered `value` (ignored if it is not currently allocated). Return the number of failed allocations.
constraints: type is 0 or 1; allocation sizes are between 1 and 2048; allocation numbers are between 0 and 200

title: Distinct Parts Partition Count
description: Count the ways to write `n` as a sum of distinct positive integers, each at most `m`, where the order of the parts does not matter. Return the count modulo `10^9 + 7`.

title: Order Statistic Replay Sum
description: A multiset starts empty. `ops` is a flat list of pairs `(type, x)`: type `0` inserts `x`, type `1` removes one copy of `x` if present (otherwise nothing happens), and type `2` asks for the `x`-th smallest element currently stored (counting duplicates, `x` starts at 1). A type-2 query contributes the answer, or `-1` if fewer than `x` elements are stored. Return the sum of all contributions.
constraints: 0 <= x <= 10^5 for types 0 and 1; 1 <= x <= 10^5 for type 2

title: Time Travel Key-Value Replay
description: A versioned key-value store is driven by `ops`, a flat list of quadruples `(type, key, value, time)`. Type `0` stores `value` under `key` at the given `time`; the times of all type-0 operations are strictly increasing in the order given. Type `1` reads `key` at the given `time` (the `value` field is ignored) and yields the value of the latest store to that key with store time at most `time`, or `-1` if there is none. Return the sum of all values yielded by reads.
constraints: 0 <= key <= 100, 0 <= value, time <= 10^6, store times strictly increase

title: Josephus Mth Eliminated
description: `n` people numbered `1` to `n` stand in a circle. Starting from person `1`, count `k` people (the starting person is counted as 1); the person reached is eliminated, and counting resumes from the next person still present. Return the number of the `m`-th person to be eliminated.

title: Smallest Level Loan Payment
description: A loan of `principal` is repaid with one fixed integer payment each month. In month `i` the balance first grows by `balance * rates[i] / 10000` (rounded down, `rates[i]` in basis points) and then the payment is subtracted. The loan is cleared once the balance is `0` or less after a payment, and it must be cleared within `rates.length` months. Return the smallest fixed payment that clears the loan.

title: Bowling Pins Removal Game
description: Bowling pins stand in a row: `s[i] = '1'` is a standing pin and `'0'` a gap. On a turn a player removes either one standing pin or two standing pins that are adjacent in the row (both must be standing). The player who cannot move loses. Return `true` if the player to move wins with perfect play.

title: Domino Placement Game Winner
description: A strip is given as a string where `.` is an empty cell and `#` is blocked. On a turn a player places a domino on two adjacent empty cells, which then become occupied. The player who cannot move loses. Return `true` if the player to move wins with perfect play.

title: Bracket Wildcard Completion Count
description: `s` consists of `(`, `)` and `?`. Count the ways to replace every `?` independently with `(` or `)` so that the result is a valid balanced bracket string (every prefix has at least as many `(` as `)`, and the totals are equal).

title: Smallest Discrete Logarithm
description: Given a prime `p` and integers `a`, `b`, return the smallest non-negative integer `x` such that `a^x` is congruent to `b` modulo `p`, or `-1` if no such `x` exists.

examples.explanation: The smallest exponent is 3 (-1 means none).
The smallest exponent is 4 (-1 means none).

title: Second Smallest Spanning Tree Weight
description: A connected undirected weighted graph has nodes `0..n-1`; `edges` is a flat list of triples `[u, v, w, ...]` with no repeated pairs. Consider every distinct spanning tree (distinct as sets of edges) and sort their total weights ascending, keeping duplicates. Return the second value in that list, or `-1` if the graph has only one spanning tree.

examples.explanation: The second smallest total weight is 7 (-1 means a unique tree).
The second smallest total weight is -1 (-1 means a unique tree).

constraints: the graph is connected, 1 <= w <= 1000, no loops, no repeated pairs

title: Optimal Search Tree Cost
description: Keys `1..n` are stored in a binary search tree and key `i` is looked up `freq[i - 1]` times. A lookup costs the depth of its key, with the root at depth `1`. Over all binary search trees on the keys `1..n`, return the smallest possible total cost, the sum of `freq[i] * depth(i)`.

title: Cut Vertex Count
description: An undirected graph has nodes `0..n-1` and edges given as a flat list of pairs `[u0, v0, u1, v1, ...]` (it may be disconnected). A node is a cut vertex if removing it (with its edges) increases the number of connected components among the remaining nodes compared with the original graph. Return how many cut vertices there are.

title: Date After Business Days
description: Business days are Monday to Friday, except for the dates listed in `holidays` (each encoded as `yyyymmdd`). Starting from the date `year-month-day` (which may itself be a weekend or a holiday), move forward `k` business days: the result is the `k`-th business day strictly after the start date, or the start date itself when `k = 0`. Return the resulting date encoded as `yyyymmdd`.
constraints: 1900 <= year <= 2100 and the start date is a valid Gregorian date
0 <= k <= 10000, 0 <= holidays.length <= 200, each holiday is a valid date between 1900 and 2100

title: Permutations With Exact Inversions
description: An inversion of a permutation is a pair of positions `i < j` holding values in decreasing order. Count the permutations of `1..n` that have exactly `k` inversions. Return the count modulo `10^9 + 7`.

title: Permutations With Exact Ascents
description: An ascent of a permutation is a position `i` with `p[i] < p[i + 1]`. Count the permutations of `1..n` that have exactly `k` ascents. Return the count modulo `10^9 + 7`.

title: Binary Trees With Bounded Height
description: Count the distinct binary tree shapes with exactly `n` nodes whose height is at most `h`. Each node may have a left child, a right child, both or neither, and left and right are distinguished. The height is the number of nodes on the longest root-to-leaf path. Return the count modulo `10^9 + 7`.

title: Kth Grid Route String
description: A walker starts at the top-left of a grid and must reach the cell `rows` steps down and `cols` steps right using only `V` (down) and `H` (right) moves. Every route is written as a string of `V` and `H`. List all distinct route strings in lexicographic order, where `H` comes before `V`, and return the `k`-th one (counting from 1).

title: Nth Smooth Number For Primes
description: Given a list of distinct primes `primes`, a number is smooth if every one of its prime factors belongs to `primes` (the number `1` is smooth). List the smooth numbers in increasing order, starting `1, ...`. Return the `n`-th one (counting from 1).
constraints: 1 <= primes.length <= 20, distinct primes below 100; the answer fits in a 32-bit signed integer
